title: Flow-Based Single-Step Completion for Efficient and Expressive Policy Learning
claim: Instead of integrating many small velocity steps along the generative path, a completion vector lets you jump from any intermediate sample straight to the target distribution.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right sequence of 5 evolving distributions, small arrows between them, long curved arrows below jumping to the end, legend with equations at right
description: A single wide panel shows five 1-D density curves in a row. The first is a smooth unimodal Gaussian labeled tau=0, in dark purple. The curves then change colour through blue and teal to green, ending in yellow at tau=1. Over this sequence the density becomes sharper and multimodal. Short purple arrows between the curves, one of them dotted, stand for step-by-step velocity propagation. Below the curves, magenta curved arrows start under each earlier curve and all land on the final curve, representing one-shot completion jumps. A legend on the right defines the velocity vector, v-hat(x_tau, tau) = h_theta(x_tau, tau, 0), in purple. It also defines the completion vector, h-hat(x_tau, tau) = h_theta(x_tau, tau, 1 - tau), in magenta. The eye goes first to the colour-graded curves, then to the long magenta arcs.
caption: Depiction of completion-based flow matching: while velocity vectors propagate along the generative path, completion vectors enable shortcut one-step jumps to the target distribution. This forms the basis of our Single Step Completion Policy (SSCP) used in offline RL and related problems.
abstract: Generative models such as diffusion and flow-matching offer expressive policies for offline reinforcement learning (RL) by capturing rich, multimodal action distributions, but their iterative sampling introduces high inference costs and training instability due to gradient propagation across sampling steps. We propose the Single-Step Completion Policy (SSCP), a generative policy trained with an augmented flow-matching objective to predict direct completion vectors from intermediate flow samples, enabling accurate, one-shot action generation. In an off-policy actor-critic framework, SSCP combines the expressiveness of generative models with the training and inference efficiency of unimodal policies, without requiring long backpropagation chains. Our method scales effectively to offline, offline-to-online, and online RL settings, offering substantial gains in speed and adaptability over diffusion-based baselines. We further extend SSCP to goal-conditioned RL, enabling flat policies to exploit subgoal structures without explicit hierarchical inference. SSCP achieves strong results across standard offline RL and behavior cloning benchmarks, positioning it as a versatile, expressive, and efficient framework for deep RL and sequential decision-making. The code is available at https://github.com/PrajwalKoirala/SSCP-Single-Step-Completion-Policy.
